# 華嚴一乘十玄門

**ID:** T1868
**Volume:** T45
**Category:** 華嚴部類
**Original Category:** 諸宗部
**Byline:** 隋 杜順說．唐 智儼撰
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 602–668
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1868

## Contributors
- 法順 (A000525)
- 智儼 (A001304)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Huáyán yī chéng shí xuán mén* is the foundational text of the Huáyán-school doctrine of the *Ten Mysterious Gates* (*shí xuán mén* 十玄門) — the ten conceptual portals through which the *Avataṃsaka*'s metaphysics of mutual interpenetration (*shìshì wú'ài* 事事無礙) is to be approached. In 1 fascicle. Per the title-line, the work was *spoken* by [杜順](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E9%A0%86) Dùshùn (the school's first patriarch) and *composed* (i.e. recorded and edited) by [智儼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%84%BC) Zhìyǎn (the second patriarch). This distinction — *Dùshùn spoke, Zhìyǎn wrote* — is the standard later-tradition account.

**Abstract**

The work is conventionally datable to Zhìyǎn's mature period at the Zhìxiāngsì 至相寺 on Mt. Zhōngnán, c. 627 – 668 CE. The bracket adopted here reflects this window. The doctrine of the *Ten Mysterious Gates* — *tóng shí jù zú* 同時具足 (simultaneity), *guǎng xiá zì zài* 廣狹自在 (vastness and narrowness), *yī duō xiāng róng* 一多相容 (mutual containment of one and many), *zhū fǎ xiāng jí* 諸法相即 (mutual identity of dharmas), *yǐn miǎn xiāng zhōng* 隱蜜相中 (manifestation and concealment), *wēi xì xiāng róng* 微細相容 (subtle mutual interpenetration), *yīntuóluówǎng* 因陀羅網 (Indra's Net), *tuō shì xiǎn fǎ* 託事顯法 (manifesting Dharma through phenomena), *shí dài bié yì* 十代別異 (ten-period differentiation), *jī yìng yuán fù* 即應圓覆 (response and complete fulfilment) — is the metaphysical core of mature Huáyán-school doctrine, fully articulated only in [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) Fǎzàng's later *[Tànxuán jì](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0008)* and *[Wǔ jiào zhāng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074)*, but already present in embryonic form here.

The *yīntuóluówǎng* / "Indra's Net" image — the cosmic net of jewels each reflecting all others — became the iconic image of Huáyán metaphysics in the East Asian Buddhist imaginary, and was elaborated by [澄觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BE%84%E8%A7%80) Chéngguān, [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) Zōngmì, and the later Korean and Japanese Huáyán/Hwaeom/Kegon traditions.

The Taishō text (T1868) is established on the standard apparatus.
